faq.q: What is Schedule 160 pipe?
faq.a: Thick B36.10M wall. NPS 6 Sch 160: OD 168.28 mm, t 18.26 mm, ID 131.76 mm, W_m ≈ 67.56 kg/m.

faq.q: What is a 6 inch flange OD in mm?
faq.a: B16.5 NPS 6 WN RF: Class 150 = 280 mm, Class 300 = 320 mm. Pipe OD is 168.28 mm — different.

title: Valve Cv Sizing Calculator
meta_description: Free valve sizing calculator — ISA/IEC US Cv for liquid & gas, Q/P1/P2, catalog Cv,sel headroom. Default liquid Cv≈80.1; docs duty Cv≈87.7.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Valve sizing calculator: liquid converts m³/h & bar to gpm/psi, Cv = Q_gpm √(SG/ΔP_psi). Gas: gauge→absolute (+1 atm), simplified non-choked screening. Adequate when calculated Cv ≤ catalog Cv,sel. Choked FL → Control Valve Choked Flow sister tool.

faq.q: What is a valve sizing calculator?
faq.a: It computes required US Cv from Q and ΔP, then checks catalog Cv,sel (adequate when Cv ≤ Cv,sel). FEK: SpecRoutes /liquid and /gas.

faq.q: Why docs Cv≈87.7 vs app default ≈80.1?
faq.a: Same Q=120 m³/h water; docs use ΔP=2.5 bar, app default uses ΔP=3 bar. Same US Cv engine.

title: Bolt Torque & Tensioning
meta_description: ASME PCC-1 flange bolt torque & tension calculation — B16.5 studs, moly T_table (K=0.13), K/grade scaling, Round 1–4. NPS 6 Cl 300 → 366 N·m.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Bolt torque / tension screening: lookup ASME B16.5 stud size/count and PCC-1-style moly T_table (K_ref = 0.13, A193 B7). Scale T = T_table × (K/0.13) × f_grade (B8/B8M Class 2 = 0.85). Four-round targets: 30% / 60% / 100% / circular 100%. First-principles tension F = σ_b·A_s is offline — confirm against the owner’s PCC-1 appendix.

faq.q: How do I do a bolt tension calculation?
faq.a: Screening path: pick NPS × class, set K and grade, read T and Round 1–4. First-principles: F = σ_b·A_s then T = K·D·F. App hero is table lookup, not live F.

faq.q: Is bolt torque the same as bolt tension?
faq.a: No. Tension is axial preload F; torque is wrench reading T. Linked by T = K·D·F when nut factor K is known.

title: Flange Bolt Tightening Sequence
meta_description: Free flange bolt torque pattern & tightening sequence generator — 12- and 20-bolt star diagrams, PCC-1 passes, even counts 4–64.

formula_json.subtitle: Star / circular bolt sequence
formula_json.formulaBasis: ASME PCC-1 legacy cross-pattern (star) torque patterns for even bolt counts 4–64, numbered clockwise from bolt 1 at top — including common 12- and 20-bolt star orders. Optional NPS × class helper fills bolt count from the same ASME B16.5 / B16.47 joint table as the Bolt Torque tool. Assembly rounds: 30% / 60% / 100% star, then 100% circular check — aligned with FEK torque screening.

faq.q: What is a 20 bolt torque pattern?
What is an 8-bolt flange star pattern?
faq.a: Number bolts 1–8 clockwise from the top. Tighten in order 1 → 5 → 3 → 7 → 2 → 6 → 4 → 8 (opposite pairs), then finish with a circular 100% pass.

faq.q: Does this replace ASME PCC-1 Appendix F?
faq.a: No. It is a field sequence diagram and Round 1–4 reminder. Use the project procedure and the Bolt Torque calculator for wrench targets.

title: Blind Flange Thickness
meta_description: Calculate ASME B31.3 / VIII-1 UG-34 flat blind thickness t = d × √(0.3P / SE) + c from diameter, design pressure, and corrosion allowance.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Required thickness uses t = d × √(0.3P / SE) + c. C = 0.30 is the ASME Section VIII Division 1 UG-34 / B31.3 para. 304.4.1 bolted flat-cover factor. d is inside or gasket contact diameter; P and S share stress units; c is corrosion allowance. Hydro blanks often omit c and use Pt.

title: Metal Weight & Cost Estimator
meta_description: Estimate metal weight and procurement cost for plate, pipe, and bar shapes using material density and unit price.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Mass = density × volume for plate, pipe, and bar. Densities are typical CS / 304 / Al / Cu screening values.

title: Stainless Steel & Special Alloy Weight & Density
meta_description: SS 316 density 8.00 g/cm³ — stainless / Duplex / Inconel plate, pipe, and bar weight. SpecRoute ss316 / ss316l.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Mass = density × volume. SS316/316L ρ = 8.00 g/cm³; SS304 = 7.93 g/cm³. Pipe volume uses OD and wall; plate/rect use L×W×t; round bar uses π/4·D²·L. Optional unit price screens material cost. Not a mill certificate substitute.

faq.q: What is the density of SS 316?
faq.a: FEK catalog SS316/316L density = 8.00 g/cm³ (8,000 kg/m³). SS304 = 7.93 g/cm³.

faq.q: Why does SS316 weigh more than SS304 for the same size?
faq.a: Typical catalog density for SS316 is about 8.00 g/cm³ versus 7.93 g/cm³ for SS304 — roughly 0.9% denser, so the same volume is slightly heavier.

faq.q: Are these densities exact for every heat?
faq.a: No. They are screening values for MTO and logistics. Use the mill certificate or ASTM / EN density for contractual mass.

title: Hydro/Pneumatic Test Pressure
meta_description: Calculate ASME B31.3 hydrostatic and pneumatic test pressure with St/S temperature correction and yield-limit screening.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Hydrostatic Pt = 1.5 × P × (St/S). Pneumatic Pt = 1.1 × P × (St/S) per ASME B31.3 para. 345.4.2. St is allowable at test temperature; S at design temperature. Default St/S = 1.0; field guide cap 6.5. Ambient CS binding 138 MPa / 20,000 psi. NPS holding-time guide: ≤2" → 10 min, 2½"–4" → 30 min, ≥6" → 60 min. Hoop vs 0.90 Sy is a site check — not computed in-app.

title: Piping Thermal Expansion & Anchor Load
meta_description: ASME B31.3 ΔL = αLΔT with guided-cantilever loop H/W and F_anchor for CS, steam pipe, CPVC, stainless, and Cr-Mo — field screening, not CAESAR II.

formula_json.formulaBasis: ΔL = α × L × (T2 − T1). Guided-cantilever H = √(3 E_h D · (ΔL/2) / S_A); U-loop W = H/2; F_anchor = 12 E_h I ΔL / H³ + μ W_pipe. CPVC uses thermoplastic α/E/S_A screening. Steam uses CS properties at elevated T2. Materials: CS, steam, CPVC, 304/316SS, Cr-Mo.

faq.q: Does this replace a flexibility analysis?
faq.a: No. It is a field screening estimate for expansion loop size and anchor load. Formal analysis is required where B31.3 flexibility rules are not obviously satisfied.

faq.q: How is CPVC handled vs steel?
faq.a: CPVC uses a much higher α (~66.6×10⁻⁶ /°C) and low E with a thermoplastic screening S_A. Confirm manufacturer ratings above ~60–93 °C.

title: Pressure Drop & Friction Loss
meta_description: Darcy–Weisbach ΔP with Haaland f, B36 ID, Crane L/D fittings, and ΔP/100 gradient. Hero includes L + Σ L_eq.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Darcy–Weisbach with Haaland friction factor. Fitting equivalent lengths use Crane TP-410 L/D (elbow 30, gate 8, globe 340). ΔP/100 is straight-only; hero ΔP includes fittings.

faq.q: Are steam and air densities fixed?
faq.a: Yes — typical screening densities. For HP steam or compressed air, treat the result as order-of-magnitude only.

title: Flow Rate & Velocity
meta_description: Pipe velocity v = Q/A vs API RP 14E vc = C/√ρ. CS/SS liquid caps and Safe / Warning / Erosion Risk screening.

formula_json.formulaBasis: v = Q/A from schedule ID (B36.10M CS / B36.19M SS). vc = C/√ρ with ρ in lb/ft³ per API RP 14E. Default C = 100 (CS) or 150 (SS). Warning if v ≥ 0.8·vc or liquid v exceeds material cap (CS ~3.5 m/s, SS ~5.0 m/s).

faq.q: What C factor should I use?
faq.a: C = 100 is the CS continuous default; C = 150 is the SS/CRA default. 125–150 is common for intermittent service — site standards prevail.

title: Quick Engineering Unit Converter
meta_description: Convert plant units: pressure, dimension, temperature, flow, torque, weight, and velocity.

formula_json.subtitle: Pressure · dimension · temperature · flow · torque · weight · velocity
formula_json.formulaBasis: Exact SI conversion factors. Torque uses 1 ft·lb = 1.355817948 N·m and 1 kgf·m = 9.80665 N·m. Mass uses the avoirdupois pound and metric tonne (1000 kg). Velocity uses 1 ft = 0.3048 m. Mass/volume flow uses the entered density (default 1000 kg/m³ water). Also available from the floating Quick Unit dock.

faq.q: Where is the floating converter?
faq.a: The ⚡ Quick Unit button stays on the lower right of every public page except this full converter.

title: Link-Seal & Penetration Sleeve Sizing
meta_description: Link-Seal modular seal sizing calculator: annular clearance C, LS model (LS-300–LS-575), link count N, and sleeve / core-drill ID from pipe OD.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Annular clearance C = (Sleeve ID − Pipe OD)/2. Select Link-Seal model whose free thickness seals C. Pitch diameter Dp = OD + 2·FT (bolt centerline for N). Ideal min sleeve ID = OD + 2·FT. Link count N = round(π·Dp / belt width). Screening ≈ 0.14 MPa / 20 psig. Independent tool — verify GPT chart; not affiliated with GPT Industries.

faq.q: How tight should Link-Seal bolts be?
faq.a: Tighten in a star pattern until the rubber links bulge slightly and contact the pipe and sleeve — do not over-torque to metal-to-metal. Follow the GPT installation sheet for the model.

title: Pipe Coping & Branch Cut Layout
meta_description: Free online pipe coping and branch cut layout calculator. Generate unwrapped flat-pattern templates and 16/32-point ordinate tables for set-on, set-in, and miter branch joints per ASME B31.3 fabrication practice.

formula_json.formulaBasis: 3D envelope intersection of branch OD with header OD (set-on/miter) or header ID (set-in). Unwrapped marking distance S = r_B·φ. Peak-to-valley cut depth Δz_max = max(z_cut) − min(z_cut). Confirm bevel and reinforcement per ASME B31.3 Para 304.3. Cut surface: z_cut(φ) from header/branch geometry.

faq.q: What is a set-on vs set-in branch cut?
faq.a: Set-on sits on the header OD surface. Set-in opens through the header wall to the ID. This tool switches the envelope radius accordingly.

faq.q: Does this replace shop lofting / CNC?
faq.a: No. It is a field screening flat-pattern and ordinate table. Verify against fabrication procedures and reinforcement calculations.

title: Pipe Branch Reinforcement Calculator
meta_description: ASME B31.3 Para. 304.3 pipe branch reinforcement calculation: area replacement A₁–A₄, pad required screening, and recommended repad thickness by header/branch NPS, schedule, and design pressure.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Required area A₁ = d₁·t_h·(2−sin β) with t = PD/(2(SEW+PY)). Available A₂/A₃ from mill-adjusted excess wall; A₄ ≈ leg_h²+leg_b². Pad when A₁ > A₂+A₃+A₄; T_pad = A_req_metal/(2 W_pad). Design temperature is for record — enter S at temperature separately.

faq.q: When is a reinforcement pad required?
faq.a: When the required area A₁ exceeds the sum of available areas A₂ + A₃ + A₄ from excess header/branch wall and fillet welds. This tool flags Pad Required when A_req > 0.

faq.q: Does this include the weld strength reduction factor W?
faq.a: Yes. Required thickness t = P·D / (2(S·E·W + P·Y)) uses W per ASME B31.3 branch reinforcement screening.

title: Pneumatic Test Safety Distance
meta_description: ASME PCC-2 Article 501 pneumatic test safety distance calculator. Screen stored energy and personnel exclusion radius for air/N2/He tests — field package starting point for inspection leads.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Ideal-gas stored energy expanding to atmosphere (gamma = 1.40 air/N2, 1.67 He): E = [P1 V /(γ−1)][1−(P0/P1)^((γ−1)/γ)]. D = R0 * (E/E_TNT)^(1/3) with R0 = 45 ft per lb TNT (~1 psi side-on unprotected personnel). Volume from direct entry or pi/4*ID^2*L. Screening only — not a blast analysis or stamped PCC-2 package.

faq.q: Does this replace a formal blast / AHJ study?
faq.a: No. It is ASME PCC-2 Article 501 field screening for an unprotected exclusion radius. Barriers, stepwise pressurization, and written authorization remain separate controls.

faq.q: How is pipe-run volume calculated?
faq.a: V = π/4 · ID² · L using ASME B36 inside diameter for the selected NPS and schedule. Add vessel or tubing volume separately when significant.

faq.q: What does R0 = 45 ft mean?
faq.a: R0 = 45 ft per lb TNT is the unprotected screening standoff for roughly ~1 psi side-on overpressure. AHJ and barrier layouts may require a larger zone.

faq.q: Why is pneumatic riskier than hydrotest?
faq.a: Compressed gas stores far more elastic energy than water. Prefer hydrostatic testing when the code and process allow.

title: Pump NPSH & Cavitation
meta_description: Mechanical pump NPSHa / cavitation margin calculator. Screen available NPSH vs OEM NPSHr for water, seawater, condensate, and light hydrocarbons (HI 9.6.1 · ASME B73.1 · API 610).

formula_json.formulaBasis: Available NPSH from absolute surface pressure, vapor pressure at pumping temperature, signed static head (flooded + / lift −), and suction losses. Margin = NPSHa − NPSHr. HI 9.6.1 margin guidance; ASME B73.1 and API 610 expect purchaser-defined margin. Screening densities and Pv curves — not a process simulator.

faq.q: What is the difference between NPSHa and NPSHr?
faq.a: NPSHa is available from the suction system. NPSHr is required by the pump at the operating capacity (OEM curve). Cavitation risk rises when NPSHa < NPSHr.

faq.q: What margin does HI 9.6.1 suggest?
faq.a: Margin is service-dependent. Many continuous cold-water duties target at least about 1.1× NPSHr; hot or volatile services need more. Confirm the project / API 610 purchaser margin.

title: Total Dynamic Head (TDH) & Pump Power
meta_description: Pump TDH and brake horsepower calculator. Screen Hs + Hf + Hp, BHP = Q·TDH·SG/(3960·η), and IEC/NEMA motor rating recommendations (HI 14.3 screening).

formula_json.formulaBasis: Total dynamic head from static elevation (signed), friction (Darcy ΔP→head), and differential pressure head. Brake power from hydraulic power / pump η (SI) or US BHP form BHP = Q·TDH·SG/(3960·η_p) (imperial). Motor input / η_m, then × service factor SF (default 1.15) before next IEC kW or NEMA HP pick. HI 14.3 is the performance-acceptance context — screening only.

faq.q: How do I get friction head Hf?
faq.a: Use the Pressure Drop calculator for ΔP, then convert Hf = ΔP / (ρ g). Include fittings and strainers.

faq.q: Does this apply HI viscosity corrections?
faq.a: No. Viscosity is shown for screening awareness. Confirm viscous duties on OEM / HI correction charts.

title: Pump Affinity Laws & Impeller Trimming
meta_description: Pump affinity laws and impeller trim calculator. Predict Q₂, H₂, P₂ from speed (VFD) or diameter cut with D₂/D₁ trimming limit warnings for TA / shutdown reviews.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Classical pump affinity for geometrically similar operation at constant efficiency: Q ∝ N·D, H ∝ (N·D)², P ∝ (N·D)³. Speed mode for VFD RPM changes; diameter mode for shop impeller cuts; combined when both change. Soft trim warning when D₂/D₁ < 0.80; hard warning below ~0.70. Screening only — confirm OEM curves, NPSHr, and motor limits after TA cuts or VFD setpoints.

faq.q: How much can I trim an impeller?
faq.a: Many centrifugal OEMs screen near 20% maximum cut (D₂/D₁ ≈ 0.80). Cuts toward 30% (D₂/D₁ ≈ 0.70) usually need manufacturer approval. Always verify the OEM trim chart.

faq.q: Do affinity laws keep efficiency constant?
faq.a: The simple affinity screen assumes η is unchanged. Real pumps often lose a few points of efficiency after a large trim or far-off-speed operation — use the OEM curve for final power.

title: Pump Minimum Continuous Stable Flow (MCSF) & Thermal Protection
meta_description: API 610 / HI 9.6.1 pump MCSF calculator. Compare thermal and hydrodynamic minimum continuous flow, estimate shut-off power, ΔT, ARC valve Cv, and bypass NPS.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Governing MCSF is the larger of thermal and hydrodynamic minima. Thermal Q_min from energy balance Q = P_so / [ρ(Cp·ΔT_max + g·H_so)] with P_so ≈ 0.5·P_rated. Hydrodynamic Q_min ≈ (0.30–0.60)·Q_BEP. ARC liquid Cv = Q_gpm√(SG/ΔP_psi). Screening only — confirm OEM MCSF and ARC vendor data.

faq.q: What is pump MCSF?
faq.a: Minimum Continuous Stable Flow is the lowest continuous capacity the OEM allows without unacceptable vibration, recirculation, or thermal rise (API 610 / HI 9.6.1). This tool screens thermal and hydrodynamic bounds; the published curve value governs.

faq.q: Why not use η in the thermal Q_min denominator?
faq.a: Energy balance at shut-off is Heat = P_so − ρgQH. Dividing H by η under-predicts thermal flow. η_min is shown only for the HI-style ΔT = gH(1−η)/(Cpη) check.

title: Multiple Pump Parallel & Series Operation
meta_description: HI 14.3 parallel and series pump calculator. Intersect quadratic pump and system curves for Q_op, H_op, flow/head gain, and runout warnings.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Quadratic pump curve H = H_so − aQ² with a = (H_so − H_rated)/Q_rated². System H = H_static + kQ² with k from friction at Q_rated. Parallel: Q_op = √((H_so − H_st)/(k + a/N²)). Series: Q_op = √((N·H_so − H_st)/(k + N·a)). Screening only — confirm OEM curves and NPSH.

faq.q: Why doesn't 2 parallel pumps double the flow?
faq.a: System friction rises with Q². The combined pump curve intersects the system at less than 2× the single-pump operating flow — often only +15–40% on friction-dominated loops.

faq.q: When do I use series instead of parallel?
faq.a: Series when static + friction head exceeds one pump's shut-off / rated head (pipeline boosters, multi-stage trains). Parallel when you need more capacity at roughly the same head.

title: Flange Bolt & Wrench Size Quick Lookup
meta_description: ASME B16.5 / B18.2.2 heavy-hex wrench AF, stud diameter, bolt count, BCD pitch, and stud length quick lookup for field spanner / socket selection.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Heavy hex nut AF from B16.5 flange bolting table (checked vs W=1.5·d_b+1/8 in). Metric AF from table mm. Stud length = RF table ± FF/RTJ delta. Pitch P_c=π·BCD/N.

faq.q: Why heavy hex instead of standard hex?
faq.a: ASME B16.5 flanges require heavy hex nuts (B18.2.2). Standard commercial hex AF is smaller — wrong wrench and under-torqued joints.

faq.q: Does facing change the wrench size?
faq.a: No. Wrench AF follows stud diameter. Facing mainly changes recommended stud length (FF shorter, RTJ longer vs RF).

faq.q: Is B16.47 (26–60") included?
faq.a: Not in this table. This lookup covers ASME B16.5 NPS ½–24 from the FEK flangeDimension.json rows.

title: Piping Insulation Thickness & Heat Loss Calculator
meta_description: ASTM C680 / ISO 12241 piping insulation heat loss Q, surface temperature Ts, and ASTM C1055 60 °C personnel protection screening for mineral wool, calcium silicate, and cellular glass.

formula_json.formulaLatex: Q = (T_h - T_a)/R_{tot},\quad R_{tot} = \ln(r_2/r_1)/(2\pi k) + 1/(2\pi r_2 h_o)
formula_json.formulaBasis: Steady radial conduction through insulation plus outer surface convection/radiation. Q = (Th − Ta)/Rtot with Rtot = ln(r2/r1)/(2πk) + 1/(2π r2 ho). ho = hc + hr; hc blends natural (1.32((Ts−Ta)/d2)^0.25) and forced wind; hr = ε σ (Ts⁴ − Ta⁴)/(Ts − Ta). k(Tm) from ASTM C533/C547-style polynomials. Personnel Pass when Ts ≤ 60 °C (ASTM C1055). Screening only — confirm jacket emissivity and manufacturer k(T).

faq.q: What surface temperature limit is used for personnel protection?
faq.a: ASTM C1055 screening uses Ts ≤ 60 °C (140 °F) for brief (~5 s) contact. Higher Ts is flagged Fail — increase thickness or add guards.

faq.q: Does this replace a certified ASTM C680 report?
faq.a: No. It is a field screening solver with app k(T) polynomials and a Churchill-style natural/forced convection blend. Confirm jacket ε, wind, and manufacturer conductivity curves for contractual work.

title: Tank & Pressure Vessel Volume Calculator
meta_description: ASME VIII Div 1 head volumes and API 650 / ISO 7507 tank level–capacity screening for horizontal and vertical vessels — partial liquid volume, fill %, ullage, and dipstick calibration.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Shell volume π r² L plus two ASME VIII Div 1 heads (flat, 2:1 SE π/24 Di³, hemi π/6 Di³, F&D/Klöpper ≈0.084766 Di³). Horizontal partial fill uses circular segment + head area-fraction strapping. Vertical fill stacks bottom head cap, cylindrical shell, and top head. Screening only — no internals; confirm certified strapping for custody transfer.

faq.q: Which head volumes does this calculator use?
faq.a: ASME VIII Div 1 screening: flat = 0; 2:1 ellipsoidal = π/24·Di³; hemispherical = π/6·Di³; torispherical Klöpper / ASME F&D ≈ 0.084766·Di³ (R=Di, r_k=0.06·Di). Head depth: 2:1 SE = 0.25·Di; hemi = 0.5·Di; F&D ≈ 0.169·Di.

faq.q: Is the dipstick table suitable for custody transfer?
faq.a: No. It is a geometric screening chart with no internals. Use API 650 / ISO 7507 certified strapping after fabrication for custody transfer.

faq.q: How is vertical partial fill computed?
faq.a: Liquid stacks from the bottom head (cap formula) through the cylindrical shell, then into the top head. Level h is from the vessel bottom; max height is 2·headDepth + L.

faq.q: Does V_total include both heads?
faq.a: Yes. V_total = V_shell + 2·V_head for both orientations. Fill % = V_liq / V_total — vertical hemi tanks often show lower fill % than shell-only rules of thumb.

title: Nitrogen Purging & Inerting Volume Calculator
meta_description: NFPA 69 nitrogen purging and inerting volume calculator for dilution-sweep and pressure-cycle pipe/vessel duties — N₂ Nm³/SCF, purge time, cycles, and cylinder supply screening.

formula_json.standard: NFPA 69 Ch.7 · API RP 2016 · CGA G-8.1
formula_json.formulaBasis: Dilution sweep uses NFPA 69-style mixing efficiency K on system volume. Pressure-cycle inerting uses absolute pressure ratio for cycle count and gauge ΔP / P_std for N₂ inventory. Piping volumes use ASME B36 Sch 40 ID. Screening only — continuous O₂ analyzer monitoring required.

faq.q: What does mixing efficiency K represent?
faq.a: K (0.25–1.0) accounts for imperfect sweep mixing. Use lower K for dead-legs or poor ventilation; 0.75 is a typical field screening default.

faq.q: Can pressure-cycle purging exceed MAWP?
faq.a: No. P_high must remain below equipment MAWP with relief protection. This tool does not check MAWP — confirm site procedure.

faq.q: Is continuous O₂ monitoring required?
faq.a: Yes per NFPA 69 / API RP 2016 practice. Theoretical volumes are screening only — verify outfall O₂ before hydrocarbons or confined-space entry.

title: ASME B16.5 Flange Pressure-Temperature Rating Calculator
meta_description: ASME B16.5 Table 2 flange pressure-temperature rating calculator for Group 1.1 carbon steel and Group 2.2 316/316L — MAWP with linear interpolation and 1.5× ambient hydrotest pressure.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Interpolate ASME B16.5 Table 2 working pressures between published temperature nodes. Hydrostatic shell test pressure = 1.5 × ambient (−29…38 °C) rating. Phase-1 tables: Group 1.1 Classes 150–2500 and Group 2.2 Classes 150/300/600. NPS ≤ 24 only — B16.47 not included.

faq.q: Which material groups are included?
faq.a: Phase-1 covers Group 1.1 (A105 / A106-B / A350 LF2) and Group 2.2 (A182 F316 / F316L). Other groups require a later data release.

faq.q: How is intermediate temperature handled?
faq.a: Linear interpolation between the nearest published Table 2 temperature nodes.

faq.q: Does this cover ASME B16.47 large flanges?
faq.a: No. Scope is ASME B16.5 NPS ½–24 only.

title: Water Density & Thermodynamic Properties Calculator
meta_description: IAPWS-IF97 / ASME steam-table water density, specific heat, viscosity, and thermal conductivity at temperature and pressure for process piping screening.

formula_json.formulaBasis: IAPWS-IF97 Region 1 subcooled liquid screening with Region 4 saturation for boiling point / phase. Viscosity and thermal conductivity use IAPWS industrial liquid-band correlations.

title: Noise Criterion Rating Calculator
meta_description: Free NC calculator — ANSI/ASA S12.2 Noise Criterion tangent rating, ASHRAE space Pass/Fail. SpecRoute control-room-nc35.

formula_json.formulaBasis: NC calculator: octave-band tangent method per ANSI/ASA S12.2. Rated NC is the lowest published NC curve (15–65) that is nowhere exceeded by measured L_p at 63–8000 Hz. ASHRAE HVAC Applications space limits drive Pass/Fail. Estimated dBA ≈ NC + 5…8 dB. Screening only — use RC/NCB for rumble or tonal isolation.

faq.q: What is an NC calculator?
faq.a: It rates room noise with the ANSI/ASA S12.2 octave-band tangent method and checks an ASHRAE space NC limit. FEK: /control-room-nc35.

faq.q: What is the NC tangent method?
faq.a: Plot octave-band SPL against standard NC curves. The NC rating is the lowest curve that is nowhere exceeded — the band that touches (or comes closest) is the tangent band.

faq.q: When should I use RC or NCB instead?
faq.a: Use Room Criterion (RC) or Balanced Noise Criterion (NCB) when low-frequency rumble or tonal noise dominates — NC alone can miss those complaints.

title: Pipe Slope & Drainage Ratio Calculator
meta_description: Pipe slope %, drainage ratio, and IPC minimum slope check from rise, run, and NPS (ASME B31.3 / IPC gravity-drain screening).

formula_json.formulaBasis: Geometric slope S = rise/run with percent, in/ft or mm/m, and 1:N ratio. IPC Table 704.1–style minimum slopes by NPS. Screening only — not for pressurized or two-phase lines.

faq.q: What is 1/4 in/ft slope as a percent?
faq.a: 1/4 in of fall per foot of run is 2.5/120 ≈ 2.08% (ratio about 1:48).

faq.q: Does IPC require 1/4 in/ft on 4 inch drains?
faq.a: IPC Table 704.1 typically allows 1/8 in/ft for 4–6 in building drains. 1/4 in/ft still complies and is a common plant drainage preference.

title: Piping Equivalent Length Calculator (Fittings & Valves)
meta_description: Crane TP-410 piping equivalent length L_eq and K-factor for elbows, tees, and valves from L/D and ASME B36 pipe ID.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Equivalent length L_eq = (L/D)×Di with Crane TP-410 L/D ratios and fully turbulent f_T. K = f_T×(L/D). Inside diameter from ASME B36.10M/B36.19M. Turbulent screening only — use 2-K/3-K for laminar or high-viscosity fluids.

faq.q: What is L/D in Crane TP-410?
faq.a: L/D is the equivalent length of straight pipe expressed as a multiple of inside diameter for a fitting or valve under fully turbulent flow.

faq.q: How is K related to L/D?
faq.a: K = f_T × (L/D), where f_T is Crane’s fully turbulent friction factor for the pipe size.

title: ISA 75.01 Control Valve Noise Prediction Calculator
meta_description: ISA/IEC control valve noise prediction: L_p,1m (dBA) from Cv, P1/P2, mass flow, and downstream pipe wall using IEC 60534-8-3 / 8-4 screening.

formula_json.formulaLatex: L_{p,1m}=L_{wA}-\Delta L_{TL}-\mathrm{RAD},\quad W_a=\eta_a W_m,\quad W_m=\tfrac12\dot m U_v^2
formula_json.formulaBasis: IEC 60534-8-3 aerodynamic and 60534-8-4 hydrodynamic screening for single-stage globe/butterfly trims. Acoustic power from jet mechanical power; pipe-wall transmission loss ΔL_TL = 17 log10(t_w/D_i)+36. External L_p,1m includes calibrated radiation and diameter corrections. Multi-stage low-noise trims require OEM attenuation tables.

faq.q: What standards does this calculator follow?
faq.a: ANSI/ISA-75.01.01 flow-capacity context with IEC 60534-8-3 (gas aerodynamic) and IEC 60534-8-4 (liquid hydrodynamic) noise screening for standard single-stage trims.

faq.q: What does L_p,1m mean?
faq.a: Predicted A-weighted sound pressure level at 1 m from the downstream pipe wall after applying acoustic power, pipe transmission loss, and radiation corrections.

faq.q: When should I use OEM noise tables instead?
faq.a: For multi-stage low-noise trims, quiet plates, diffuser silencers, or special cage designs — FEK screening assumes standard single-stage globe/butterfly geometry.

title: ISO 5167 Orifice Plate Flow & Pressure Drop Calculator
meta_description: ISO 5167-2 orifice plate mass/volumetric flow and permanent pressure loss from beta ratio, Δp, and Reader-Harris/Gallagher discharge coefficient C.

formula_json.formulaBasis: ISO 5167-2 Reader-Harris/Gallagher discharge coefficient with flange/corner/D-D2 taps. Liquid screening uses ε = 1. Permanent loss ≈ Δp(1−β^1.9). Valid for 0.1 ≤ β ≤ 0.75 and Re_D ≥ 5000 with adequate straight lengths per §6.2.

faq.q: What is the beta ratio β?
faq.a: β = d/D_i, the orifice bore divided by the pipe inside diameter. ISO 5167-2 screening is valid for roughly 0.10 ≤ β ≤ 0.75.

faq.q: What is permanent pressure loss Δϖ?
faq.a: The non-recoverable head loss across the orifice run, approximated as Δp·(1−β^1.9) for screening.

faq.q: Which tap type should I select?
faq.a: Flange taps are the common process default. Corner and D–D/2 taps change L1/L2' in the Reader-Harris/Gallagher C equation.

title: Darby 3-K Fitting Loss Calculator (Laminar & Turbulent K-Factor)
meta_description: Darby 3-K fitting resistance coefficient K and equivalent length L_eq from K1, Ki, Kd across laminar to turbulent Reynolds numbers, with Crane TP-410 comparison.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Darby 3-K resistance coefficient with laminar K1/Re and size-scaled turbulent Ki term. Equivalent length uses Crane fully turbulent f_T so L_eq compares with TP-410 L/D screening. Pipe ID from ASME B36.10M/B36.19M.

faq.q: What is the Darby 3-K method?
faq.a: A Reynolds-number-aware fitting loss model: K = K1/Re + Ki·(1 + Kd/Din^0.3). It covers laminar through fully turbulent flow better than constant Crane L/D factors.

faq.q: When should I prefer Darby 3-K over Crane TP-410?
faq.a: Use Darby 3-K for laminar or transitional Re (especially Re < 2000) and when pipe size scale effects matter. Crane L/D is a turbulent-flow screening shortcut.

faq.q: How is L_eq calculated from K?
faq.a: L_eq = K·Di/f_T using Crane’s fully turbulent friction factor for the NPS, so lengths compare with TP-410 equivalent-length tables.

title: IAPWS-IF97 Steam Thermodynamic Properties Calculator
meta_description: IAPWS-IF97 steam enthalpy, entropy, density, and saturation temperature for saturated and superheated steam screening (Region 2 / Region 4).

formula_json.formulaBasis: IAPWS-IF97 industrial formulation for Region 2 superheated steam and Region 4 saturation (wet/dry quality x). Viscosity and thermal conductivity use IAPWS industrial transport correlations. Critical / Region 3 states are out of scope.

faq.q: What steam states does this calculator cover?
faq.a: Region 4 saturation (quality x from 0 to 1) and Region 2 superheated steam up to the critical pressure Pc = 22.064 MPa. Supercritical and Region 3 states need a full ASME steam table.

faq.q: What is steam quality x?
faq.a: Dryness fraction: x = 0 is saturated liquid, x = 1 is dry saturated vapor. Wet steam properties are linear mixtures of hf/hg, sf/sg, and vf/vg.

faq.q: How is enthalpy calculated?
faq.a: From the IAPWS-IF97 dimensionless Gibbs free energy: h = R·T·τ·(γ_τ⁰ + γ_τʳ) in Region 2, with saturated states evaluated on the Region 4 line.

title: Pipe Support Span Calculator (ASME B31.3 & B31.1 Chart)
meta_description: ASME B31.3 Para. 321 pipe support span from deflection and sustained bending, with ASME B31.1 Table 121.5–style chart compare and ASME B36 pipe weight.

formula_json.formulaLatex: L_{def}=(384 E I y_{max}/(5 w_{total}))^{1/4},\quad L_{str}=\sqrt{10 Z S_{allow}/w_{total}},\quad L_{rec}=\min(L_{def},L_{str},L_{chart})
formula_json.formulaBasis: Uniform dead-weight span screening per ASME B31.3 Para. 321. L_def uses simply-supported deflection; L_str uses continuous-span bending M ≈ wL²/10 with S_allow = 0.5 S_h. Layout recommendation is the lesser of beam theory and the ASME B31.1 Table 121.5–style support spacing chart (also common in MSS hanger guides). Pipe OD/ID/weight from ASME B36.10M/B36.19M; stainless weight scaled by density.

faq.q: What governs the recommended support span?
faq.a: The hero span is the lesser of beam-theory L_beam = min(L_def, L_str) and the B31.1 Table 121.5–style chart. For water-filled carbon steel at the default 12.7 mm mid-span limit, the chart usually governs layout.

faq.q: How does this relate to MSS hanger spacing charts?
faq.a: The chart values match ASME B31.1 Table 121.5 and the same numbers commonly reprinted in MSS hanger guides. Beam-theory spans are shown for comparison; prefer the more conservative chart for layout unless analysis justifies a longer run.

faq.q: When should I shorten the calculated span?
faq.a: Reduce spans near concentrated loads (valves, heavy flanges, strainers), elbows and tees, and in high-vibration or slug-flow service per ASME B31.3 Para. 321 guidance.

title: Control Valve Choked Flow & xT / FL Screening Calculator
meta_description: ISA-75.01.01 / IEC 60534-2-1 control valve choked flow and liquid cavitation screening with x_T, F_L, F_k, and ΔP_max limits.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Choked-flow and cavitation screening per ANSI/ISA-75.01.01 (IEC 60534-2-1 Mod) §5 for standard trims without reducers (F_P = 1). Gas uses x vs F_k·x_T; liquid uses ΔP vs F_L²(P1 − r_c·Pv) with r_c = 0.96 − 0.28√(Pv/Pc).

faq.q: When is gas flow choked?
faq.a: When the pressure differential ratio x = (P1−P2)/P1 reaches or exceeds x_choked = F_k·x_T. Flow then caps at ΔP_max = x_choked·P1.

faq.q: What is F_L used for?
faq.a: F_L is the liquid pressure recovery factor. Cavitation screening uses ΔP_cav = F_L²(P1 − r_c·Pv). If actual ΔP ≥ ΔP_cav, cavitation risk is flagged.

faq.q: Are these absolute or gauge pressures?
faq.a: Absolute pressures (bar abs / psia). Convert gauge to absolute before entry (add atmospheric pressure).

title: PSV / PRV Orifice Area Screening Calculator (API 520 / API 526)
meta_description: API 520 Part I / API 526 PSV orifice area screening for gas and liquid with standard effective orifice letters D through T.

formula_json.standard: API 520 Part I / API 526 / ASME VIII UG-131
formula_json.formulaLatex: A_{req}=\frac{W}{C K_d P_1}\sqrt{\frac{TZ}{M}}\ (\mathrm{gas}),\quad A_{req}=\frac{Q}{38 K_d}\sqrt{\frac{G}{\Delta P}}\ (\mathrm{liquid})
formula_json.formulaBasis: Critical gas/vapor sizing per API 520 Part I §5.2 and non-viscous liquid sizing per §5.6 (Kd = 0.975 gas / 0.650 liquid; Kb = Kw = Kv = Kc = Z = 1 for atmospheric discharge screening). Selected orifice is the smallest API 526 Table 1 effective area ≥ A_req (letters D–T).

faq.q: What orifice letter does this calculator return?
faq.a: The smallest API 526 standard effective orifice (D through T) whose area is at least the API 520 required area A_req.

faq.q: Are Kd values certified?
faq.a: No. Screening uses API 520 preliminary Kd = 0.975 (gas) and 0.650 (liquid). Certified ASME UG-131 nameplate Kd from the manufacturer must be used for purchase.

faq.q: Does this include backpressure or two-phase flow?
faq.a: No. Atmospheric discharge and single-phase screening only. Built-up/superimposed backpressure, HEM two-phase, and viscosity (Kv) are out of scope.

title: Natural Gas Compressibility Z-Factor & Density Calculator
meta_description: Natural gas compressibility Z-factor and real density screening from Standing Ppc/Tpc, Hall-Yarborough Z, and the real-gas law (AGA 8 / CNGA screening).

formula_json.standard: AGA Report No. 8 / API MPMS 14.2 / Standing–Hall–Yarborough / CNGA
formula_json.formulaLatex: \rho=\frac{P\cdot SG\cdot M_{air}}{Z\cdot R\cdot T},\quad T_{pc}=168+325\,SG-12.5\,SG^{2},\quad P_{pc}=677+15\,SG-37.5\,SG^{2}
formula_json.formulaBasis: Standing sweet-gas pseudo-criticals with optional Wichert-Aziz CO2 and Kay N2 blend; Z from Hall-Yarborough (CNGA fallback); density from the real-gas law. Screening only — AGA-8 Detail / GERG-2008 composition EOS out of scope.

faq.q: What Z method is used?
faq.a: Standing Ppc/Tpc with Wichert-Aziz (CO2) and Kay (N2), then Hall-Yarborough with CNGA fallback.

faq.q: Is absolute pressure required?
faq.a: Yes. Enter bar abs or psia — not gauge — unless you add atmospheric pressure yourself.

faq.q: When is AGA-8 Detail required?
faq.a: For custody transfer, P ≳ 150 bar, supercritical transport, or LNG envelopes — verify with full composition EOS.

title: Heat Exchanger LMTD & Duty Calculator
meta_description: TEMA LMTD, F-factor correction, heat duty, and required area with IAPWS-IF97 water/steam properties for shell-and-tube screening.

formula_json.standard: TEMA 9th Ed. Sec. 5 / IAPWS-IF97 / API 660 screening
formula_json.formulaLatex: \Delta T_{lm}=\frac{\Delta T_1-\Delta T_2}{\ln(\Delta T_1/\Delta T_2)},\quad \Delta T_{lm,corr}=F\,\Delta T_{lm},\quad A=Q/(U\,\Delta T_{lm,corr})
formula_json.formulaBasis: Counterflow LMTD with TEMA 1–2n / multi-shell F-factor. Water/steam enthalpy from IAPWS-IF97. Screening only — not a TEMA mechanical design or HTRI rating.

faq.q: What F-factor method is used?
faq.a: TEMA / Bowman closed-form F for 1 shell–2n tube passes, with N-shell series mapping of P.

faq.q: When is F < 0.75 a problem?
faq.a: Below F ≈ 0.75 the temperature approach is too steep for a practical 1-shell unit — increase shell passes or reduce effectiveness.

faq.q: How is steam condenser duty calculated?
faq.a: When Th,in ≈ Th,out, Q = ṁ · h_fg at IAPWS saturation temperature equal to the hot terminal.

title: Compressor Gas Power & Polytropic Screening Calculator
meta_description: GPSA polytropic head, gas power, and discharge temperature for centrifugal/axial compressor screening per API 617 and ASME PTC 10.

formula_json.standard: GPSA Sec. 13 / API 617 / ASME PTC 10 screening
formula_json.formulaLatex: H_p=\frac{Z_{avg} R T_1}{M}\frac{n}{n-1}\left[r_p^{(n-1)/n}-1\right],\quad P_{gas}=\frac{\dot m H_p}{\eta_p},\quad T_2=T_1 r_p^{(n-1)/n}
formula_json.formulaBasis: Polytropic exponent from (n−1)/n = (k−1)/(k η_p). Gas power from mass flow × polytropic head / η_p. Screening only — not an OEM performance map or PTC 10 acceptance test.

faq.q: What polytropic efficiency range is typical?
faq.a: Centrifugal compressor polytropic efficiencies commonly fall near 60–88%. This tool accepts 40–95% for screening.

faq.q: When is multi-stage compression recommended?
faq.a: When single-stage r_p > 4.5 or discharge temperature exceeds ~150 °C (API 617 seal/gas-quality screen), split stages with intercooling.

faq.q: Is constant Z_avg enough at high pressure?
faq.a: Above ~50 bar(a) discharge, confirm Z with Lee–Kesler or RK EOS — constant-Z screening may understate head.

title: API 650 Tank Shell Thickness Calculator (1-Foot Method)
meta_description: API 650 Section 5.6.3 1-foot method shell course thickness, Table 5.2a/5.2b minimums, commercial plate selection, and shell MTO screening.

formula_json.formulaLatex: t_d=\frac{4.9 D (H-0.3) G}{S_d E}+CA,\quad t_t=\frac{4.9 D (H-0.3)}{S_t}+CA,\quad t_{nom}=\mathrm{CeilPlate}(\max(t_d,t_t,t_{min}))
formula_json.formulaBasis: API 650 1-foot method design and hydrotest shell thickness by course. H is liquid height above the bottom of the course. Screening only — Variable-Design-Point (§5.6.4), wind girders, and seismic buckling are out of scope.

faq.q: When is the 1-foot method not allowed?
faq.a: API 650 §5.6.3 limits the 1-foot method to tanks with D ≤ 60 m (200 ft). Larger tanks require the Variable-Design-Point Method (§5.6.4).

faq.q: How is commercial plate selected?
faq.a: t_required = max(t_d, t_t, t_min). t_nom is the next standard mill plate thickness at or above t_required.

faq.q: Are wind girders included?
faq.a: No. This tool sizes shell courses for product and hydrostatic head only. Intermediate wind girders and seismic buckling need a separate API 650 check.

title: Olet Fitting Dimensions & Branch Sizing (Weldolet / Sockolet / Threadolet)
meta_description: MSS SP-97 Weldolet, Sockolet, and Threadolet dimensions with run-size match, cutout diameter, and B31.3 branch t_b screening — not a pad area replacement.

formula_json.formulaBasis: MSS SP-97 envelope dimensions (A, B, d_hole, J) by olet type and outlet rating. Run NPS must fall in the consolidated run-size range. Optional branch design thickness t_b uses B31.3 §304.1.2 with screening S for A105 / A182 F316. Does not replace §304.3.2 area replacement.

faq.q: Does this replace B31.3 area reinforcement?
faq.a: No. Use Pipe Branch Reinforcement for A1/A2 pad checks. This tool looks up MSS SP-97 olet envelopes only.

faq.q: Why do Weldolets use STD/XS while Sockolets use Class 3000?
faq.a: Weldolet ends match pipe schedule wall; Sockolet and Threadolet are forged to pressure class (MSS SP-97 / B16.11 family).

faq.q: What if run size shows Fail?
faq.a: The selected header NPS is outside the screening consolidated run range for that outlet. Confirm size-on-size or OEM specials before ordering.

title: Pipe Steam / Heat Tracing Duty & Steam Consumption
meta_description: ISO 12241 insulated pipe heat loss with IAPWS saturated steam h_fg — steam consumption (kg/h per 100 m) and tracer line count for winterization / process maintain screening.

formula_json.standard: ISO 12241 · IAPWS-IF97 · Spirax Sarco Heat Tracing Design Manual (screening)
formula_json.formulaBasis: Radial insulation heat loss from ASTM C680 / ISO 12241 solve (same engine as Insulation Heat Loss). Saturated latent heat h_fg from IAPWS-IF97 at gauge+atm absolute pressure. Tracer count from bare-contact capacity K·(Tsat−Tmaint). Screening only — confirm OEM charts, cement, and trap spacing.

related.title: Steam Properties (IAPWS)
related.carry: Saturated steam h_fg at supply pressure

faq.q: Is this for superheated steam tracers?
faq.a: No. Use saturated steam supply. Superheat reduces condensation heat transfer and can create local hot spots.

faq.q: Does heat-transfer cement reduce tracer count?
faq.a: Yes — cement can raise capacity about 3–4× versus bare contact. This screen assumes bare contact.

faq.q: Why report steam use per 100 m?
faq.a: Field trap and loop segmentation typically review duty on ~100 m runs; scale linearly for shorter segments.

title: Socket Weld & Threaded Fitting Dimensions (ASME B16.11)
meta_description: ASME B16.11 forged socket-weld and threaded fitting dimensions — center-to-end A, socket B/J, wall G, band OD, B31.3 SW gap, and B1.20.1 thread engagement L₂.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Envelope dimensions A/B/J/G/C from ASME B16.11 forged fitting tables (SW Class 3000/6000/9000; threaded Class 2000/3000/6000). NPT L₂ from B1.20.1. Socket weld gap g_sw = 1.5 mm per B31.3 Para. 328.5.2. Screening only — confirm OEM chart.

faq.q: Why is Class 2000 missing for socket weld?
faq.a: ASME B16.11 Class 2000 applies to threaded fittings only. Socket-weld ratings start at Class 3000.

faq.q: What is the socket weld gap?
faq.a: B31.3 requires about 1.5 mm (1/16 in) between the pipe end and the socket bottom after insertion to absorb weld expansion.

faq.q: Does this cover NPS above 4?
faq.a: Regular B16.11 forged SW/THRD fittings stop at NPS 4. Larger sizes are specials outside this chart.

title: Pressure Vessel Head Thickness (ASME VIII-1 UG-32)
meta_description: ASME Section VIII Div.1 UG-32 formed head thickness — 2:1 ellipsoidal, torispherical, hemispherical, and conical t_req / t_nom with II-D allowable stress S(T).

formula_json.standard: ASME Section VIII Division 1 UG-32 (d–g) · Section II Part D Table 1A (screening)
formula_json.formulaLatex: t_{req}=\frac{P D}{2SE-0.2P}\ (2{:}1),\quad t_{req}=\frac{0.885 P L}{SE-0.1P}\ (tori),\quad t_{nom}=t_{req}+C.A.
formula_json.formulaBasis: Internal (concave-side) pressure thickness for formed heads per ASME VIII-1 UG-32(d) ellipsoidal, (e) torispherical with L=D, (f) hemispherical with R=D/2, (g) conical without knuckle α≤30°. Allowable stress S from Section II-D Table 1A screening curves. Screening only — not UG-22 loads or UG-28 external pressure.

related.title: Pipe Wall Thickness
related.carry: Same design pressure / temperature / material family

related.title: Pressure Vessel Nozzle Reinforcement
related.carry: Same shell ID / design pressure / temperature / material

faq.q: Does this cover external pressure / vacuum?
faq.a: No. UG-32 addresses internal pressure on the concave side. External pressure and vacuum use UG-28 charts.

faq.q: Why is torispherical thicker than 2:1 ellipsoidal?
faq.a: UG-32(e) with L=D uses a 0.885 crown factor that yields greater t_req than UG-32(d) for the same P, D, S, and E.

faq.q: What does t_nom include?
faq.a: t_nom = t_req + corrosion allowance. It is the nominal design thickness before mill under-tolerance or forming thinning checks.

title: Pressure Vessel Nozzle Reinforcement Pad (ASME VIII-1 UG-37)
meta_description: ASME Section VIII Div.1 UG-37 / UG-40 nozzle opening area replacement — required A vs available A1–A42, repad thickness screen with II-D allowable stress S(T).

formula_json.standard: ASME Section VIII Division 1 UG-37 / UG-40 / UG-41 · Section II Part D Table 1A (screening)
formula_json.formulaLatex: A=d t_r F+2 t_n t_r F(1-f_{r1}),\quad A_{avail}=A_1+A_2+A_3+A_{41}+A_{42}
formula_json.formulaBasis: Internal-pressure area replacement for openings in shells and formed heads per ASME VIII-1 UG-37 (required area), UG-40 (limits of reinforcement / available area), and UG-41 (strength of reinforcement with f_r ≤ 1). Allowable stress S from Section II-D Table 1A screening curves. Screening only — not WRC 107/537/297 local stresses or UG-28 external pressure.

related.title: Pressure Vessel Head Thickness
related.carry: Same shell ID / design pressure / temperature / material

related.title: Pipe Branch Reinforcement
related.carry: Related area-replacement concept for B31.3 branch openings

related.title: Pipe Wall Thickness
related.carry: Same design pressure / temperature / material family

faq.q: Does Pass mean no pad is required?
faq.a: Pass means A_avail ≥ A with the entered pad (t_p may be zero). If the engine reports a non-zero minimum pad thickness, excess shell/nozzle metal alone is insufficient without added pad metal.

faq.q: Are WRC local stresses included?
faq.a: No. This tool covers UG-37 internal-pressure area replacement only. Piping loads and nozzle local stresses require WRC 107/537/297 or equivalent.

faq.q: When is f_r2 less than 1.0?
faq.a: When nozzle allowable stress is below shell allowable (S_noz / S_shell < 1). Available nozzle wall and inward-projection areas are reduced by f_r2.

title: Rolling Element Bearing Life L10h Calculator (ISO 281 / ABMA 9)
meta_description: ISO 281 / ABMA 9 & 11 bearing L10h rating life calculator — equivalent dynamic load P = X·Fr + Y·Fa, L10 = (C/P)^p, L10h hours at 90% reliability for ball and roller bearings.

formula_json.formulaLatex: P=X F_r+Y F_a,\quad L_{10}=(C/P)^p,\quad L_{10h}=\frac{10^6}{60 n}L_{10}
formula_json.formulaBasis: Basic rating life at 90% reliability per ISO 281 and ABMA 9 (ball) / ABMA 11 (roller). Equivalent dynamic load P = X·Fr + Y·Fa with catalog or screening X,Y factors. Life exponent p = 3 (ball) or 10/3 (roller). Modified life L10mh with a_ISO lubrication/contamination factors is out of scope — screening only.

faq.q: What is L10h?
faq.a: Basic rating life in hours at 90% reliability — the life that 90% of a group of identical bearings are expected to achieve or exceed under the stated duty.

faq.q: When do I use p = 3 vs 10/3?
faq.a: Ball bearings use p = 3. Roller bearings (cylindrical, spherical, tapered) use p = 10/3 ≈ 3.333 per ISO 281 / ABMA.

faq.q: Does this include a_ISO modified life?
faq.a: No. This tool reports basic L10h only. Lubrication, contamination, and material factors for L10mh require ISO 281 a_ISO review with OEM catalog data.

title: Lifting Lug & Rigging Capacity Calculator (ASME BTH-1 / AISC)
meta_description: ASME BTH-1 Category B / AISC lifting lug capacity screen — sling P_t and P_s, pin-hole bearing, tear-out shear, and base fillet weld unity for pad-eye design.

formula_json.standard: ASME BTH-1-2023 · AISC Steel Construction Manual · ASME B30.20 · AWS D1.1
formula_json.formulaLatex: P_t=W_{lift}\cdot IF/(N\cos\theta),\quad \sigma_b=P_t/(D_{pin} t)\le 1.25 F_y/N_d,\quad \tau_w=\sqrt{(P_t/A_w)^2+(P_s h/S_w)^2}\le 0.30 F_{EXX}
formula_json.formulaBasis: ASME BTH-1 Design Category B (Nd = 2.0) pin-hole bearing, AISC-style lug tear-out, and both-face fillet weld combined shear/bending at the lug base. Screening only — not a stamped BTH-1 / B30.20 lift package. Sling angle from vertical limited to 60°.

faq.q: What is Design Category B Nd = 2.0?
faq.a: ASME BTH-1 Design Category B uses design factor Nd = 2.0 on yield for the pin-hole bearing and related lug plate checks in this screen.

faq.q: Why is sling angle capped at 60° from vertical?
faq.a: Angles above 60° from vertical produce large lateral components and buckling risk outside this pad-eye screen — use a spreader / lifting beam and a stamped design.

faq.q: Is weld stress based on one-face or both-face fillet?
faq.a: This app models both-face fillet welds along the lug base length (A_w = 2 · 0.707 · w · L), which is standard pad-eye practice.

title: Steam Turbine Power Output & Specific Steam Consumption Calculator (ASME PTC 6 / IAPWS-IF97)
meta_description: ASME PTC 6 / IAPWS-IF97 steam turbine power and SSC screen — isentropic enthalpy drop, shaft and electrical MW, specific steam consumption, and condensate heat-rate estimate.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Single-pressure steam turbine expansion using IAPWS-IF97 Region 2 inlet and isentropic exhaust at P2. Screening only — no reheat or multi-extraction heat balance.

faq.q: What is SSC?
faq.a: Specific steam consumption — main steam mass per unit electrical energy (kg/kWh or lb/kWh).

faq.q: Does this include reheat?
faq.a: No. This is a single-pressure expansion screen. Reheat and extraction balances need OEM / process-simulator tools.

faq.q: What moisture limit is flagged?
faq.a: Exhaust moisture above about 12% raises a warning for last-stage blade erosion risk.

title: Shaft Power, Torque & Parallel Key Sizing Calculator (DIN 6885 / ASME B17.1)
meta_description: DIN 6885-1 / ASME B17.1 shaft torque and parallel-key shear/bearing screen — transmitted torque, key length L_min, and unity ratios for pure torsion duty.

formula_json.standard: DIN 6885-1 · ISO R773 · ASME B17.1 · AGMA 6001
formula_json.formulaBasis: Pure-torsion shaft shear and parallel-key shear/bearing length screening. DIN 6885-1 key sizes (metric) or ASME B17.1 square keys (imperial). Bending moment and keyseat Kt fatigue are out of scope.

faq.q: Which standard sizes the key?
faq.a: Metric duties use DIN 6885-1 parallel keys by shaft diameter band. Imperial duties use ASME B17.1 square-key screening sizes.

faq.q: What is h1 in the bearing check?
faq.a: Keyseat contact depth in the shaft is taken as h1 ≈ 0.5·h for the compressive stress formula.

faq.q: Does this include bending from overhang?
faq.a: No. Pure torsion only. Significant overhang moments need combined stress and keyseat Kt review.

title: Storage Tank Venting Rate Calculator (API 2000 7th Ed)
meta_description: API Std 2000 7th Ed normal inbreathing/outbreathing and fire-exposure emergency vent capacity for atmospheric and low-pressure metal storage tanks — PVRV screening.

formula_json.formulaBasis: API 2000 §3.3 liquid and thermal normal venting plus §3.4 fire emergency capacity for vertical cylindrical tanks. Screening only — not thermal shock or reactive gas cases.

faq.q: What does normal outbreathing include?
faq.a: Liquid pump-in displacement plus thermal expansion outbreathing (API 2000 §3.3).

faq.q: How is wetted area limited?
faq.a: Vertical-tank wetted height for fire is capped at 9.14 m (30 ft) per API 2000 §3.4.

faq.q: Is this a certified PVRV selection?
faq.a: No. It is a field screen of required free-air rates — confirm OEM PVRV / hatch charts.

title: ASME B16.34 Valve Wall Thickness & Pressure Rating Calculator
meta_description: ASME B16.34 Standard Class valve body minimum wall thickness (Appendix VI / Table 3) and P-T rating screen with hydrostatic shell test pressure.

formula_json.standard: ASME B16.34-2020 §6.1 · Table 3 · Table 2 · Mandatory Appendix VI
formula_json.formulaBasis: Standard Class valve body minimum wall from Appendix VI (S=7000 psi, A=0.10 in) with Table 3 discrete check, plus Standard Class P-T rating and 1.5× ambient hydro shell test. Special Class and Section 8 NDE rules are out of scope.

faq.q: What is t_m in ASME B16.34?
faq.a: Minimum valve body wall thickness from Table 3 / Appendix VI for the class designation pressure P_c and inside diameter d.

faq.q: Does Standard Class P-T match B16.5?
faq.a: For the same material group, ASME B16.34 Standard Class ratings align with B16.5 Table 2. Phase-1 FEK extract covers Groups 1.1 and 2.2.

faq.q: Is Special Class included?
faq.a: No. Special Class and Section 8 NDE / forged high-pressure rules are out of this screen.

title: Safety Relief Valve (PSV) Reaction Force Calculator (API 520 Part II)
meta_description: API RP 520 Part II open-discharge PSV reaction force screen — momentum and exit pressure thrust with dynamic load factor for vapor/gas service.

formula_json.standard: API RP 520 Part II (2015) §4.2 · ASME VIII-1 Appendix M
formula_json.formulaBasis: Open-discharge vapor/gas reaction force from sonic exit momentum plus exit static pressure thrust, scaled by DLF for popping. Liquid and two-phase out of scope.

faq.q: What is PSV reaction force?
faq.a: The thrust on the discharge piping when a safety valve pops — momentum of the jet plus any exit pressure above atmosphere, often amplified by a dynamic load factor.

faq.q: Why use DLF = 2.0?
faq.a: API 520 Part II recommends up to 2.0 for sudden popping on open vent elbows as a screening dynamic amplification.

faq.q: Does this cover liquid relief?
faq.a: No. Liquid and two-phase cases need separate transient piping analysis.

title: Non-Metallic Flat Gasket Dimensions & Sealing Area Calculator (ASME B16.21)
meta_description: ASME B16.21 nonmetallic flat gasket OD/ID from B16.5 geometry with VIII-1 Appendix 2 Wm2 seating load and m/y factors for IBC and full-face sheets.

formula_json.formulaBasis: IBC ring uses B16.5 raised-face OD × B36 pipe OD. Full face uses flange OD with B16.5 bolt circle. Wm2 = Ag·y; Wm1 uses App. 2 G, b, m, P.

faq.q: What is an ASME B16.21 flat gasket calculator?
faq.a: A lookup of nonmetallic sheet gasket OD/ID for B16.5 flanges plus Appendix 2 seating load Wm2 from Agasket and y.

faq.q: IBC vs full face?
faq.a: IBC (ring) seats on the raised face. Full face covers the flange face and includes bolt holes on the B16.5 pitch circle.

faq.q: Is B16.47 covered?
faq.a: Not in Phase-1. Large-diameter B16.47 Series A/B tables are out of the local flangeDimension extract.
